doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Billy Butterfield albums and too much reverb
summary: After an audio clip, Conniff says on 'Just Kiddin' Around' with Billy Butterfield he went overboard with reverb.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I had noticed, I’m not sure I have this cued up to —
Oh that’s Billy Butterfield, “Just Kiddin’ Around,” isn’t that the name?
I noticed in this particular recording, as opposed to some of the other albums, that there was just a lot more reverb.

I went overboard. I’ll be honest with you. We did two albums, Billy Butterfield and I. One was called [coughs extensively] We did two albums with Billy Butterfield. One was called “Conniff Meets Butterfield,” and the other was called “Just Kiddin’ Around.” The first one was very successful and a real fun album, and I tried to do the same thing. You never quite can do the same thing again. And I felt after I heard that back I felt I went overboard with the reverb a little bit. It’s exciting, but I don’t know, I think if I did it over I’d either do a little different reverb or not quite so much, I don’t know which. But now I can’t remember what got us into that.
